title_fr: Oscillations libres d'un circuit RLC série
caption_fr: Glisse R, L, C : observe les trois régimes, la trace u_C(t) et l'échange d'énergie C↔L. Mets R≈0 pour le régime non amorti.
url_note: The ?ctz= payload is the LZString.compressToEncodedURIComponent encoding of circuit_import_text (Falstad's standard share-link format). Auto-generated by the orchestrator and round-trip-verified (decompressFromEncodedURIComponent reproduces the netlist exactly); should be eyeballed once in a browser at the editorial gate. The plain circuit_import_text below remains the authoritative source — if the URL ever fails, load it via File → Import From Text in CircuitJS.
circuit_import_text_notes: $ 1 ... : header — timestep 1 µs; simulation speed factor 10.17; viewport 64×50 grid units at 50 px/unit.
r 192 160 → 384 160 : resistor R = 5 Ω on the top rail (horizontal). Drag this value to explore regimes.
l 384 160 → 384 352 : inductor L = 0.1 H on the right rail (vertical). Initial current = 0 A (capacitor discharged into L, not L into nothing).
c 384 352 → 192 352 : capacitor C = 10 µF on the bottom rail (horizontal). Initial voltage = 6.0 V (condensateur préchargé).
s 192 352 → 192 160 : normally-open switch K on the left rail (vertical). Student clicks to close — starts the free discharge oscillation.

O lines: voltage output probes (label-only nodes, Falstad type O flag 1 = no current drawn). Optional; remove if they cause import warnings — the student can add scope probes by right-clicking any component.

component_values.notes: T₀ = 2π√(LC) = 2π√(0.1 × 10⁻⁵) = 2π × 10⁻³ s ≈ 6.28 ms. ω₀ = 1/√(LC) = 1000 rad/s. E_C(max) = ½ × 10⁻⁵ × 36 = 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ J. These match the spec §5 worked-number seeds exactly.

param_manipulation_guide.R: Change by right-clicking the resistor component → Edit → set resistance. Three teaching presets: (1) R≈0.1–1 Ω — near-undamped sinusoid, régime périodique (quasi non amorti). (2) R≈5 Ω — lightly damped, pseudo-périodique (default, netlist value). (3) R = 200 Ω — seuil critique / apériodique: this is R_c = 2√(L/C) = 2×√(0.1/10⁻⁵) = 2×√(10⁴) = 2×100 = 200 Ω exactly. At R = R_c the circuit is critically damped — u_C returns to zero without oscillation as fast as possible; above it the decay is purely exponential. Dragging R does NOT change the peak spacing (T₀ fixed by L and C alone) — only the decay rate changes. This is the R3 confrontation.
param_manipulation_guide.L: Change by right-clicking the inductor → Edit. Increasing L increases T₀ = 2π√(LC). Decreasing L speeds up the oscillation. Demonstrates M3/M4: period depends on L, not R.
param_manipulation_guide.C: Change by right-clicking the capacitor → Edit. Same effect as L on T₀. Also changes the initial stored energy E_C = ½CU₀².

scope_setup_instructions: After importing, right-click the capacitor and select 'View Voltage in Scope' to see u_C(t). Right-click the inductor and select 'View Voltage in Scope' to see u_L(t). Right-click anywhere on the wire to 'View Current'. The scope shows live traces; adjust the simulation speed slider (bottom) so the full oscillation is visible. For the energy view, right-click the capacitor scope trace and select 'Show Power' — this gives ½Cu² proportional energy. The C↔L antiphase exchange is visible when both C voltage and L current are scoped simultaneously.

pedagogy_wiring.R3_predict_then_reveal: Before the student touches the slider: 'Prédit ce qui se passe quand R→0.' M1 student predicts oscillation stops. Close switch → observe damped trace. Then lower R to 0.1 Ω → perfect sinusoid. Then raise R to 200 Ω → apériodique. The embed IS this confrontation.
pedagogy_wiring.M2_M7_energy: Scope u_C(t) on capacitor AND current on a wire. When u_C is maximal, current is zero (all energy in C). When u_C is zero, current is maximal (all energy in L). The antiphase is directly visible on the dual-trace scope.
pedagogy_wiring.M3_M4_period: Hold R fixed, drag L or C — period changes visibly. Then hold L and C fixed, drag R — period does not change, only decay rate changes.
pedagogy_wiring.placement: Engine of rung R3 (predict-then-reveal on R). Revisited at R4 (three regimes), R6 (trace-reading, measure pseudo-période off scope). Calm core — no reward animation, no score, no engagement theater.

boundary: free oscillations + entretien only — NO forced/driven-frequency sweep, NO résonance curve, NO impédance readout
boundary_compliance_notes: The netlist contains NO AC voltage source, NO function generator, NO driven-frequency element. The only source is the pre-charged capacitor (initial condition U₀=6 V) — free oscillation only.
The switch K starts open. Closing it initiates free discharge. There is no external periodic driving force.
Falstad's CircuitJS does expose an AC source element in its component palette — but none is placed in this circuit. The renderer/teacher must not add one.

If entretien is to be demonstrated (rung R7), replace R with a dependent voltage source delivering u_G = k·i (a VCVS in Falstad, gain = k). Set k = R_value to cancel damping. This is a SEPARATE configuration, not included here — it involves no frequency sweep and no résonance; it restores the free undamped regime at T₀.

The analytic damped solution (exp(−αt)·cos(ω_D·t)) is computed internally by Falstad for display — this is fine: the spec allows DISPLAYING the damped trace (qualitative/experimental view). The LESSON must not derive or formularise it (LIMITE 1). The embed is a viewing instrument; the derivation boundary is the lesson author's responsibility.
No impédance, no phaseur, no AC power readout is present or accessible in this configuration.
fallback_note: If this embed is not wired in time: C1 (static traces, svg+katex) + C3 (energy diagram, svg+katex) with 3 pre-set parameter snapshots (R≈0 / R=5Ω / R=200Ω) carry the load for R3/R4/R6. The manipulable is the intended primary; degradation is graceful per spec §3.
